chunks: He [al-Mufid] said: Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad al-Katib informed me, who said: al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abd al-Karim al-Za'farani informed me, who said: Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi narrated to us, who said: Isma'il ibn Aban informed us, who said: Amr ibn Shimr narrated to us, who said: I heard Jabir ibn Yazid say: I heard Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali, peace be upon them both, say: My father narrated to me, from my grandfather, peace be upon them both, who said:

When the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, set out from Medina toward the oath-breakers at Basrah, he stopped at al-Rabadhah. And when he departed from there, Abdullah ibn Khalifa al-Ta'i met him, having stopped at a place called Qudayd. So the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, drew him close. Abdullah said to him: Praise be to Allah who restored the right to its owners and placed it in its proper place, whether some people disliked it or were pleased by it. For by Allah, they hated Muhammad, peace be upon him, opposed him, and fought him, but Allah turned their plot back upon their own throats and made the circle of evil fall upon them. And by Allah, we shall surely fight alongside you in every situation, in protection of the Messenger, may Allah bless him and his family and grant him peace.

So the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, welcomed him and seated him beside himself, for he was a beloved friend and ally. He began asking him about the people until he asked him about Abu Musa al-Ash'ari. He said: By Allah, I do not trust him, nor do I feel safe from his opposition if he finds a supporter in that. The Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said to him: By Allah, he was never trustworthy in my estimation nor sincere. Those who preceded me had won his loyalty, appointed him, and given him authority over the people. I intended to dismiss him, but al-Ashtar asked me to keep him, so I kept him despite my reluctance, and I undertook to dismiss him later.

He said: While he was with Abdullah discussing this and similar matters, suddenly a great multitude appeared from the direction of the mountains of Tayy. The Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said: Look! What is that multitude? So the horsemen rode out galloping and did not delay before returning. It was said: This is Tayy! They have come to you driving sheep, camels, and horses. Among them are those who came with gifts and hospitality, and among them are those who wish to march out with you against your enemy. The Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said: May Allah reward Tayy well, 'And Allah has favored those who strive over those who sit back with a great reward.'

When they reached him and greeted him, Abdullah ibn Khalifa said: I was pleased, by Allah, by what I saw of their assembly and the beauty of their appearance. They spoke and confirmed their commitment. By Allah, I have not seen with my own eyes an orator more eloquent than their orator. Adi ibn Hatim al-Ta'i stood up, praised Allah and lauded Him, then said: As for what follows, I embraced Islam during the time of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant him peace, and I paid the zakat during his time, and I fought the people of apostasy after him. I sought by that what is with Allah, and upon Allah is the reward of whoever does good and is God-fearing. And it has reached us that men from the people of Makkah have broken your pledge and opposed you unjustly. So we have come to you to support you upon the truth. We are before you, so command us as you wish. Then he recited: And we helped Allah before that / And you came to us in truth, so you shall be helped / We shall suffice you against all the people entirely with our might / And you are more deserving of it than all other people.

The Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said: May Allah reward you, O tribe, on behalf of Islam and its people, with good. For you submitted willingly, fought the apostates, and intended to help the Muslims.

Sa'id ibn Ubayd al-Bahtari from the tribe of Bahtar stood up and said: O Commander of the Faithful, indeed among people there are those who are able to express with their tongue what is in their heart, and among them are those who cannot articulate what they find within themselves with their tongue. If he forces himself to do so, it is difficult for him, and if he stays silent about what is in his heart, grief and distress torment him. And indeed, by Allah, not all that is in my heart can I convey to you with my tongue. But by Allah, I shall strive to make it clear to you, and Allah is the guardian of success. As for me, I am a sincere adviser to you in secret and in public, and a fighter alongside you against the enemies in every situation. I see for you rights that I did not see for those who came before you, nor for anyone today of the people of your time, because of your merit in Islam and your kinship with the Messenger. And I shall never part from you until you triumph or I die before you. The Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said to him: May Allah have mercy on you, for your tongue has expressed what your conscience conceals for us. And we ask Allah to grant you well-being and reward you with Paradise.

And some men among them spoke, but I did not remember other than the words of these two men. Then the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, departed and six hundred men from among them followed him until he arrived at Dhu Qar, where he encamped with one thousand three hundred men.

key_terms.أَبُو مُوسَى الْأَشْعَرِيّ: Abu Musa al-Ash'ari: Governor of Kufa whose loyalty to Imam Ali was questioned
key_terms.النَّاكِثِين: Oath-breakers: those who broke their pledge of allegiance to Imam Ali, referring to the leaders of the Battle of the Camel
key_terms.جَنْگ جَمَل: Battle of the Camel: the first civil war in Islam (656 CE) between Imam Ali and the forces at Basrah
key_terms.ذَا قَار: Dhu Qar: a staging area in southern Iraq where Imam Ali gathered his forces
key_terms.عَدِيّ بْن حَاتِم: Adi ibn Hatim: a prominent companion, chief of the Tayy tribe and one of Imam Ali's strongest supporters

ai.seo_question: What happened when Imam Ali marched from Medina to Basrah and met the Tayy tribe?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates Imam Ali's march from Medina toward Basrah to confront the oath-breakers (the Battle of the Camel). Along the way, he is met by Abdullah ibn Khalifa al-Ta'i, who pledges full military support. They discuss Abu Musa al-Ash'ari's untrustworthiness. The Tayy tribe then arrives in force with gifts and fighters. Adi ibn Hatim al-Ta'i delivers a powerful speech recounting his acceptance of Islam, his loyalty through the Ridda Wars, and his readiness to fight the rebels, concluding with a poem of commitment. Another tribesman, Sa'id ibn Ubayd, delivers an emotionally sincere speech about his inability to fully express his devotion, vowing never to leave Ali's side. Imam Ali responds graciously to both, and the narrative concludes with his arrival at Dhu Qar with 1,300 men. This hadith provides a rare glimpse into the political dynamics, tribal alliances, and personal loyalties that shaped the early Islamic period after Uthman's assassination.

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 6. He said: Abul Hasan ‘Ali ibn Muhammad al-Katib reported to me from al-Hasan ibn ‘Ali ibn Abdul Karim al-Za’farani, who reported from Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi, who reported from Ismail ibn Aban, who reported from Amru ibn Shimr, who said: I heard Jabir ibn Yazid reporting from Abu Ja’far Muhammad ibn ‘Ali, peace be upon him, who reported from his father, and from his grandfather, peace be upon them all,

that when Amirul Mu’mineen, peace be upon him, left Madinah for Basrah to confront the renegades, he stopped at al-Rabdhah. And then as he left from there, he was met by Abdullah ibn Khalifa al-Taee, at a place called Qudaid. Amirul Mu’mineen, peace be upon him, welcomed him. Then Abdullah said:"Praise be to Allah who restored the right to its owner and kept it in its rightful place, regardless of whether some people were pleased or displeased. By Allah, they had hated Muhammad, peace be upon him and his progeny, resisting and fighting against him. But Allah turned their guile against them, and made the disaster to befall them. By Allah, we shall fight by your side in every situation, protecting (the message of) the messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his progeny."

Amirul Mu’mineen, peace be upon him, welcomed him and made him sit by his side, for he was indeed his helper and friend. Then he started inquiring about people till he mentioned Abu Musa al-Ashari. He said: "By Allah, I do not trust him, and I do not see you secure against him if he finds support." Amriul Mu’mineen, peace be upon him, replied: "By Allah, he was neither trustworthy nor a good counsel in my estimation. But those who preceded me were captured by his fancy and gave him authority to govern the people. And I had decided to remove him, but al-Ashtar asked me to confirm him, so I did it reluctantly. Thereafter, I had to sustain his dismissal."

He said: He (i.e. Amirul Mu’mineen) remained with Abdullah this way, till a great multitude was seen coming from the mountains of Tay. Amirul Mu’mineen said: "Look out, who are they?" So, some of the horsemen ran to find out, and soon came back to report that they were the people of Tay who had come with their sheep and camels and horses. Some of them had come with their gifts for ‘Ali, and some intended to go with him to fight his enemy. So Amirul Mu’mineen, peace be upon him, said: "May Allah reward the people of Tay a good reward, and ’He (i.e. Allah) has a far richer reward for those who fight for Him than for those who stay at home.’[4:95]"

And when they drew close to him, they greeted him. Abdullah ibn Khalifa said: "By Allah, I was pleased with what I experienced from their group, and by their excellent form. They spoke and confirmed their stand. By Allah, I have not seen a more eloquent speaker than their spokesman." And Adi ibn Hatim al-Taee stood up, praised Allah and lauded Him and then said: "I had embraced Islam in the days of the Prophet, peace be upon him and his progeny, and I paid my Zakat (dutifully) in his time, and after he had departed, I fought the apostates. I did all that to earn the pleasure of Allah, and indeed, the reward of one who does good and guards against evil is from Allah. We are informed that some men of Makkah have reneged on your loyalty, and have turned against you as aggressors. So we have come to help you on the right path, and here we are, before you. So command us to do whatever you wish." Then he recited the following: "And we have helped (the cause of) Allah before you, and you have come to us with truth, so you will be helped. All of us shall be sufficient for you against them all, And indeed, of all man, you deserve this most."

Then Amirul Mu’mineen, peace be upon him, said: "May Allah reward you on behalf of Islam among all living people, and on behalf of all Muslims. You have indeed submitted voluntarily and fought the apostates, and are determined to help the Muslims."

Then Saeed ibn Ubaid al-Bahtari from the tribe of Bani Bahtar rose and said: "O Amirul Mu’mineen, some men are able to say what they have in their minds, while others are unable to express what they think in their hearts. And if they are forced to do it, they find it extremely difficult. And if they keep silent, the grief torments them and makes them restless. As far as I am concerned, I can not convey to you all that I have in my mind, but I will try my best to be explicit, and Allah is the custodian of success! I am surely your best counsellor, privately and in open, and I will fight by your side in every situation; and I see you with the Truth, the way I never saw those who preceded you, nor any other person among your contemporaries! This is because of your merit and excellence in Islam, and your relation to the Prophet. I shall never part from you till you win, or I die before you." Amirul Mu’mineen, peace be upon him, said: "May Allah bless you with mercy, Your tongue has indeed expressed what you conscience has concealed. I pray to Allah that He may bless you with good health, and reward you with Paradise."

Then others from them spoke, but I do not remember the speech of any other but these two men. Then Amirul Mu’mineen decamped, and from them six hundred followed him till they reached Zuqar. When he arrived there, he had One thousand and three hundred men.
